object_description: square compact five-storey block around a five-storey introverted inner courtyard
design_condition: the compact square block is precisely positioned on the building lines and deliberately set back from the neighbouring high-rise, its recessed ground floor forming a lounge towards the street

positive: The recessed ground floor lounge and the parapet-form top floor create a striking, distinctive volume
The square compact structure is precisely positioned on the building lines
The building is deliberately set back from the high-rise staff building
The project fits into the existing situation in urban planning and volumetric terms
The materialisation and structuring of the interior give a good interior quality and identity-creating character
The homely design of the common rooms on the attic floor is particularly effective
The five-storey inner courtyard with learning islands as cantilevered terraces forms the heart of the complex
Its interesting spatial structure contains the actual communication spaces and access routes
The large skylight allows natural lighting
A well-dimensioned double spiral staircase in the core gives access to all floors
Placing the public lounges on the attic floor results in an attractive situation
The concept with administration and large classrooms on the ground floor and others above is practical and functional
Natural lighting of the basement laboratories is guaranteed by the deepening of the site
Delivery and bicycle cellar access via the eastern inner courtyard work well
The load-bearing system with a core supporting the slab structure allows the required flexibility
The relatively compact volume has good floor area ratios
The building is self-confident from both an urban planning and architectural point of view
The attractiveness of the public spaces is enhanced by the expression and interior atmosphere
negative: The adjustable vertical slats in front of the storey-high glazing give the building a rather introverted character
The inner courtyard is totally introverted with no references to the outside via the facade
Natural lighting is restricted on the lower floors by the narrowing of the terraces
Placing library and canteen on the attic floor leads to long access routes to these public-intensive uses
Basement lighting will be impaired depending on the height of the future neighbouring building
Some facade and roof constructions and interior glazing are more complex
Construction costs are in the upper segment
The introverted nature of the building is only partially able to meet the objectives of the school
